PROCEDURE
Preparation of 100 ml of decinormal Na2C03 solution A.
Heat some pure anhydrous sodium carbonate in a porcelain basin for some time so as to expel all the moisture. Cool it and then place in a desiccator.
Accurately weigh out about 0.53 gm of Na2C03 by placing it on a watch glass. Note the weight taken.
Transfer all the particles of Na2C03 into the volumetric flask quantitatively with the help of the funnel. Wash down the particles left on the watch glass with distilled water.
Dissolve the Na2C03 with a little distilled water. The solution should not splash while dissolving the solute.
Then add distilled water upto the neck of the flask through the funnel.
Remove the funnel and add more water dropwisely with the help of a pipette so that the lower meniscus of the solution coincides the mark of the volumetric flask.
Close the flask with its lid and shake the solution.
Standardization of H2S04 solution using standard NazC03 solution Wash the whole apparatus with water.
Clean the burette with distilled water and rinse it with the given acid.
Practical Chemistry Clamp the burette vertically to the stand so that the jet of the burette remains slightly above the mouth of the conical flask. Fill the bUrette with acid upto the zero mark.
Clean the pipette with distilled water. Rinse the pipette with the standard Na2C03 solution.
Pipette out 10 ml of standard alkali into a clean conical flask. Add 2-3 drops of methyl orange and shake gently.

Take the first reading by running out 1 ml of the acid at a time from the burette into the alkali taken in the conical flask. Shake the flask during each addition giving the rotatory motion to the solution into the flask.
Appearance of slight permanent pink colour in the solution indicates that the solution has acquired the end point of Efrat-ion. Note the volume of the acid in the burette.
Wash the conical flask with distilled water. Pipette out 10 ml of the alkali into the conical flask.
Titrate the alkali against H2S04 solution as before.

During the process of titration, a state will come when you cannot say definitely whether the solution in the conical flask is colourless or very faint yellow. It may or may not be end point. To check the end point, note the volume of the acid in the burette and add a drop of the acid carefully into the conical flask.
